reflection_text.7:
The board is A-D x 1-5. White D1-D2 is a two-stone group with the single shared liberty D3 because D1 is already in contact with C1 black and D2, D2 is adjacent to C2 black, D1 white and the empty D3. C3-C4 also uses D3. So any first white move ≠ D3 is met by 1…B D3 and White loses D1-D2 at once. The forced defence is therefore 1.W D3, which joins D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. B5 and D5 stay separate.

After the forced 1.W D3 the three black shapes are
A2 : A1 A3 B2
B3-B4 : A3 B2 A4
C1-C2 : B1 B2
The only connecting move is B2. After 1…B B2 the three shapes become the single group
S = A2-B2-B3-B4-C1-C2
with the four distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1. Any white probe on those four points is itself in atari on the paired liberty and Black can recapture the probe and keep ≥2 liberties, e.g. 2.W B1 2…B A1, 2.W A1 2…B B1, 2.W A3 2…B A4, 2.W A4 followed by 2…B A1/A3/B1 and a recapture on A5. Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5 or 2.B D4 which gives the white D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 group the single shared liberty D4/C5 and prevents any forcing net on the left. Hence after the forced defence no first white move forces a capture of a black group against best defence.

The isolated corner net arguments for {B1} and {B2} are flawed once the D1-D2 atari and suicide rules are applied. After 1.W B1 the C1-C2 group is indeed reduced to B2 and B2 is illegal for Black because B2 would be surrounded by A2 black, B1 white, B3 black, C2 black and would not capture B1 – B1 still has A1. The same move also lets Black play 1…B D3 and capture the D1-D2 group for free, so B1 is not a forcing killer. The same D3 refutation applies to any first move ≠ D3. The claim that B2 is the shared vital point is true in isolation, but 1.W B2 is also met by 1…B D3 which keeps all black groups alive, and after the forced 1.W D3 the classic A-file squeeze is no longer forced because S has four liberties and Black can always recapture a probing stone.

Unresolved tension is whether a sacrifice of D1-D2 should be admissible. Under the usual survival reading the D3 capture is a legitimate defence that lets Black’s groups live, so the set of killing initiators is empty. The {B1} and {B2} camps rely on ignoring the D1-D2 atari and/or on treating B2 as legal after W B1. With suicide correctly evaluated and the forced defence taken into account the defensible outcome is {}.
reflection_text.3:
The position is the classic left-corner net. Black has the three interlocked shapes
A2 : A1 A3 B2
B3–B4 : A3 B2 A4
C1–C2 : B1 B2
and White has B5, C3, C4, D1, D2, D5. The decisive points are A1, A3, A4, B1, B2.

Round 0 split is B1 as the classic forcing first point and B2 as the double-atari vital point, with a minority {} claim. The previous reflection already noted the D1–D2 liberty issue: on a normal sized board D1–D2 has E1/E2/D3, so White is not forced to defend on the first move, and the standard net is 1.W B1 1…B B2 2.W A3/A4 with a forced A1–A3–A4 squeeze. B2 was also argued as the shared liberty of the three black shapes.

Current round 1 changes the picture because a large group of colleagues now treats the diagram as a minimal 4×5 board with corner A1. On a 4×5 board D is the bottom edge and col5 the right edge. Then

D1 : C1 black, D2 white
D2 : D1 white, C2 black, D3 empty

so the White two-stone group D1–D2 has the single liberty D3. Any first White move ≠ D3 is met by 1…B D3 and White loses D1–D2. Hence the only legal defence is 1.W D3, which joins D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. B5 and D5 stay separate and share C5/D4.

After the forced 1.W D3 Black can connect the three black shapes with 1…B B2, giving the merged A2–B2–B3–B4–C1–C2 group the four distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1. White can only probe A1/A3/A4/B1 and each probe is recapturable, e.g. 2.W A1 2…B B1, 2.W A3 2…B A4, etc. The same defence also allows Black to attack the newly formed White group with 1…B C5 or 1…B D4 after 1.W D3, exploiting the shared liberties C5/D4 of D1–D2–D3–C3–C4, B5 and D5. Under the minimal-board interpretation the classic B1/B2 net is not available because White’s first move is forced to D3 and the A-file squeeze is no longer forced.

Conversely, colleagues 11,12,15,17,3,4 continue to argue for {B1} under the normal-board assumption, and colleagues 13,14,16,2,5,6,8,9 argue for {B2} as the unique vital point that creates immediate atari on C1–C2 and forces B1. The B1 camp highlights 1.W B1 1…B B2 forcing and the A1–A3–A4 squeeze, with the claim that B2 after W B1 is illegal/suicide. The B2 camp highlights 1.W B2 puts C1–C2 on B1 and makes W B2 itself in atari on B1, forcing 1…B B1 and then 2.W A1 2…B A3 3.W A4.

The key unresolved issue is board size / the liberty of D1–D2. The problem states “on a board with corner labelled A1” but does not state the board is larger than the extreme coordinates used. If the board is taken as minimal 4×5 the forced 1.W D3 defence kills the net and the set of killing initiators is empty. If the board is taken as a normal / essentially infinite board where E1/E2 exist, White is free to play in the corner and the classic net is available, with the literature and Round 0 consensus favouring B1 as the unique forcing first move, B2 being the commonly cited but weaker double atari.

Unresolved questions: is the board to be read as minimal 4×5 or as a standard Go board with only the shown area relevant? That decision determines whether the correct initiator set is {} or {B1} / {B2}.
reflection_text.11:
The D1-D2 atari dominates the opening. White D1-D2 is a two-stone group whose only external liberty is D3, which is also the shared liberty of the C3-C4 group. Hence 1…B D3 wins D1-D2 immediately and any first White move ≠ D3 is losing. The forced first move is therefore 1.W D3, joining D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. 

After 1.W D3 Black’s three corner shapes are A2 : A1 A3 B2, B3-B4 : A3 B2 A4, C1-C2 : B1 B2. The only unifying defence is 1…B B2, which makes S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with the four distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1. White probes A1, A3, B1 are all one-liberty probes that Black can immediately recapture by occupying the paired liberty A1↔B1, A3↔A4, and the A4 probe leaves S with A1 A3 B1 and the white A4 stone with A3 A5. In all cases Black can keep S with ≥2 real liberties and can recapture any attacking white stone, e.g. 3.W A4 4…B A1/B1 leaves S on A3 B1 or A1 A3 and White A4 is met by Black A5 capturing the net. Other Black replies after 1.W D3 such as C5 or D4 give the white D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 group a single shared liberty and prevent any forcing net on the left.

The earlier B1/B2 net arguments assume White can start on the left side. They fail because 1.W B1 or 1.W B2 is met by 1…B D3 and White loses D1-D2 at once. The claimed “suicide/illegal B2 after W B1” and the classic A1-A3-A4 squeeze are therefore irrelevant once the forced D3 defence is respected. The D3-forced line shows no first White move can force a later capture of any Black group against best defence; the set of killing initiators is empty. The remaining disagreement in the room is whether the B2 sacrifice can be made after D3, but the forced D3 move removes the tempo needed for that net.
reflection_text.17:
The board is 4 columns A-D by 5 rows 1-5 with A1 the corner. With that geometry E is off-board.

White D1-D2 is a two stone edge group. D1 is on the right edge next to C1 black and D2 white, D2 is next to C2 black, D1 white and D3 empty. Its only liberty is D3. White C3-C4 shares D3. Hence 1…B D3 captures D1-D2. The only legal first move that does not lose D1-D2 at once is

1.W D3

which joins D1-D2-D3-C3-C4. After 1.W D3 the merged white group has the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. White B5 and D5 stay separate but are linked to the same liberties.

That forced defence removes the classic B1/B2 corner net from the first move. After the forced 1.W D3 Black’s best defence is 1…B B2 connecting

A2-B2-B3-B4-C1-C2

into one group with distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1. The group now has four real liberties and White can probe at most one per move. Any probe on A1 is recaptured by B1, any probe on B1 is recaptured by A1, any probe on A3 is matched by A4 etc., and White’s own A4 probe is met by A5 recapture that restores the group’s liberties. Black can also attack the white side by 1…B C5/D4 and keep the D4/C5 net on the White D1-D2-D3-C3-C4-B5-D5 complex.

Colleagues 1,10,18 correctly identify the forced 1.W D3 defence and show that after 1.W D3 Black can keep the merged A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 group with ≥2 liberties and can always recapture a White probing stone on A1/A3/B1/A4. The D3 defence is the reason the {} position arguments are valid on a 4×5 board.

The B1-first and B2-first lines cited in round 0 and by Colleagues 11-12-15-17-3-4 and Colleagues 13-14-2-5-6-8-9 respectively assume White is free to play B1/B2 on move one. Those lines ignore the one-liberty atari on D1-D2 and the forced 1.W D3. Once the forced defence is taken into account B1 and B2 are no longer available as first moves and the net on A1-A3-A4 is not forced. The earlier A5 recapture objection to the B2 net and the suicide/legality disputes about B2 after W B1 are now moot because the move order is pre-empted by D3.

Current belief: with best defence Black can keep the A2/B3-B4/C1-C2 groups alive after the forced 1.W D3, and no White first move initiates a forced killing sequence of the Black corner. The set of killing initiators is empty.
reflection_text.16:
The corner shape is the classic A-file net. Black stones are A2 : A1 A3 B2, B3-B4 : A3 A4 B2, C1-C2 : B1 B2. B2 is the common liberty of the three black shapes and B1 is the last liberty of C1-C2.

W B1 puts C1-C2 in atari on B2. B2 is now a point with three black neighbours A2,B3,C2 and one white neighbour B1, so 1…B B2 is suicide and does not capture B1 because B1 still has A1. Hence C1-C2 cannot be saved and 2.W B2 captures C1-C2. After the capture the remaining A2 and B3-B4 are left with the A1-A3-A4 net and the whole mass is dead.

W B2 puts C1-C2 in atari on B1 and puts the sacrificial stone W B2 in atari on B1. The only legal saving reply is 1…B B1, which captures W B2 and joins B1 to C1-C2. The three black shapes are now under simultaneous pressure on the A file and the classic A1-A3-A4 squeeze is forced; any other black reply loses C1-C2 immediately to 2.W B1.

The D1-D2 self-defence objection requires a 4-column board on which E1 is off board. On a normal Go board D1-D2 has E1,D3,E2 liberties and White is not forced to play D3 first, so the left-corner net is viable. Both B1 and B2 initiate a forced killing net; B1 is the capture-forcing first cut and B2 is the vital-point sacrifice. The set of forcing first moves is therefore B1 and B2.
reflection_text.4: The board is not about D1-D2. D1–D2 has E1/E2/D3 liberties so the “D3 is forced” argument is a misread. The three black collections are A2 : A1 A3 B2, B3–B4 : A3 B2 A4, C1–C2 : B1 B2. B1 puts C1–C2 on the single liberty B2 and is not immediately capturable. After 1.W B1 Black is forced to 1…B B2 otherwise 2.W B2 captures C1–C2 at once. After 1.W B1 1…B B2 the merged A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 group has the three distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 and White B1 now lives on A1. 2.W A4 reduces the black group to A1 A3 and gives White A4 the liberties A3 A5. 3…B A1 is the capture of the atari White B1, giving the black group the liberties A3 B1 and White A4 the liberties A3 A5. 4.W A5 connects A4 to the existing white B5 and creates the extra breathing on the A-file. 5…B A3 is now forced, leaving the black group with the single liberty B1. 6.W B1 captures the whole A1 A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 mass. The same net is obtained if Black tries 3…B A3 after 2.W A4, because 4.W A1 then captures the whole merged group. Any first white point other than B1 either loses immediately to a Black connection on B2 or fails to force the A1–A3–A4 squeeze; in particular W B2 is a self-atari sacrifice that lets Black answer B1 and restores ≥2 liberties to the merged group, and the D-file defence is a red herring. The unique forcing initiator is therefore B1.
reflection_text.1:
The discussion is now split between a board-edge reading and an unlimited-board reading. The edge reading, which is the one used in the persistent memory, takes A1 as the bottom-left corner and D5 as the top-right corner, i.e. a 4×5 board. Under that reading White D1–D2 has the unique liberty D3 and C3–C4 also needs D3, so Black wins D1–D2 on the next move unless White defends immediately. Hence 1.W D3 is forced. After 1.W D3 the white D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 group has liberties D4,C5 and White B5,D5 stay separate. Black’s only useful reply is the connection 2.B B2 which unifies A2, B3-B4 and C1-C2 into S = {A2,B2,B3,B4,C1,C2} with the four distinct liberties A1,A3,A4,B1. Any White probe on those four points is a one-liberty probe which Black can answer by occupying the paired liberty and capturing the probe stone, e.g. W B1 B A1, W A1 B B1, W A3 B A4, W A4 B A1/A3, and S never falls below two real liberties. Black can also keep White busy on the right with 2.B C5/D4, so White never obtains a forced capture of S. That is the {} argument made by Colleagues 1,10,18 in round 1 and by Colleagues 1,10,18 in round 0.

The {B1} and {B2} camps assume the board is not edge-limited at D/E. Under that larger-board reading D1–D2 is not in one-liberty atari and White is not forced to play D3 on move 1. The classical corner net is then invoked: B2 is the shared liberty of A2, B3-B4 and C1-C2 and White B2 puts C1-C2 in atari on B1 while making the sacrifice itself one-liberty on B1, so Black is forced to 1…B B1 to save C1-C2. After 1.W B2 1…B B1 the black C1-C2-B1 chain has liberties A1,B2, A2 has A1,A3,B2 and B3-B4 has A3,A4,B2. The camp claims a forced A1-A3-A4 squeeze follows, with 2.W A1/A3/A4 leading to a capture of the merged mass. The {B1} camp makes the symmetric claim that 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 in atari on B2, forces 1…B B2, and then the A1-A3-A4 net is forced.

The edge reading explains why those nets are illusory in the stated puzzle. After the forced 1.W D3 Black’s 2.B B2 connection gives S four liberties and the B1/B2 suicide/legality claims used by the {B1} camp disappear once the connection to A2,B3,C2 is taken into account. Moreover, the claim that B2 is legal after W B1 on an edge-limited board is correct: B2 connects to A2,B3,C2 and the merged group retains liberties A1,A3,A4, so B2 is not suicide. The same connectivity makes the alleged forced double atari on A1/A3/A4 after 1.W D3 2.B B2 impossible: White can at most occupy one of A1,A3,A4,B1 per move and the probe stone is itself in atari on the remaining liberty and is captured by Black.

Unresolved is the exact board size stipulation. The problem statement only says “on a board with corner labelled A1”, which formally allows a larger board. If the board were unbounded to the north/east the D3 defence would not be forced and the classic B2 net would be available in the abstract. Under the minimal 4×5 interpretation that is consistent with all given coordinates and with the persistent memory, White has no first move that initiates a forced killing sequence; the only legal first move is the defensive 1.W D3. reflection_text.12:
The board is at least A–D × 1–5 so the D1-D2 white two-stone group has the outside liberties E1/E2 in addition to D3; the D-file self-defence argument is therefore a red herring and White is not forced to play D3 before attacking the corner. The decisive fighting is the A-file corner net on A2, B3-B4 and C1-C2.

* 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 into one liberty on B2. B2 is the only saving point for C1-C2 and B2 is not suicide after B1, so 1…B B2 is forced. After 1.W B1 1…B B2 the three black shapes are one with the three net liberties A1 A3 A4 and White B1 is in atari on A1. 2.W A4 removes A4 and leaves the black mass on A1 A3. Black is forced to 2…B A1 to take the atari B1; the capture gives the black mass the two liberties A3 B1 and White A4-A3 then forces B1 on the next move, i.e. a forced A1-A3-A4 squeeze. The sequence is a clean net and B1 is a forcing first move.

* 1.W B2 is the shared liberty of A2, B3-B4 and C1-C2. After 1.W B2 C1-C2 is 1-liberty on B1 and the sacrificing W B2 itself is 1-liberty on B1, so 1…B B1 is forced to save C1-C2 and it captures the sacrifice. After 1.W B2 1…B B1 the C1-C2-B1 chain is on A1 B2, A2 is on A1 A3 B2 and B3-B4 is on A3 A4 B2. The continuation 2.W A4 forces Black to B2, after which White A3 leaves the merged black mass with the single liberty A1 and White A1 captures. The same net is obtained with 2.W A3; in either case Black can only meet on B2 and the A-file squeeze is forced. B2 is the sacrificial vital point and also initiates a forced kill.

A1 is a probe which is immediately met by B2 and does not create a forced two-liberty net. The D1-D2 defence issue is not relevant on a board large enough for E1/E2. The two forcing initiators are therefore B1 and B2. 

The set of killing initiators is {B1,B2}.
reflection_text.10:
The discussion remains split on board size.  The minimal 4×5 interpretation used in the previous round still forces White’s first move on the D1-D2 two-stone shape.  On a board that ends at D the D1-D2 group has the single liberty D3, so 1.W D3 is forced; after 1.W D3 the White D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 group has the two distinct liberties D4 and C5 and White B5/D5 remain separate.  Black can then unify A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 by 1…B B2 to the group A2-B2-B3-B4-C1-C2 with the four distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1.  Any White probe on A1/A3/A4/B1 is met by Black occupying the paired liberty and recapturing the probing stone, e.g. 3.W B1 4.B A1, 3.W A1 4.B B1, 3.W A3 4.B A4, etc., so the merged Black group never falls below two real liberties and Black can also answer 1.W D3 by 2.B C5/D4 to give the White D-group the single shared liberty D4/C5.  With best defence Black therefore keeps the A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 mass alive and no first White move forces a capture of a Black group.

The alternative infinite-board reading removes the D1-D2 self-atari.  Under that reading D1-D2 has E1/E2/D3 liberties and White is not forced to play D3.  On an unlimited board the classic vital point of the left corner is B2: 1.W B2 puts C1-C2 into 1-liberty atari on B1 and puts the sacrificial W B2 into atari on B1, so Black is forced to 1…B B1 capturing the sacrifice.  After 1.W B2 1…B B1 the three Black shapes are under simultaneous A-file pressure and the subsequent 2.W A3/A4, 2…B B2, 3.W A4 type squeeze forces Black into a self-atari on A1.  The same shape is often quoted with the sacrificial first move B1, 1.W B1 1…B B2 being the usual way the net is described, and many colleagues list B1/B2 as the forcing initiator.  The disagreement is therefore essentially about the board edge: with the minimal 4×5 board assumed in the first round the D3 defence is forced and the set of killing initiators is empty, namely {}.  If the board is taken as unlimited the conventional net point is B2, with B1 being the sacrificial equivalent quoted in the literature.
reflection_text.15:
The position is the classic A-file corner net. Under the
usual infinite-SE reading the three black shapes are

* A2 : A1 A3 B2
* B3-B4 : A3 B2 A4
* C1-C2 : B1 B2

and W D1-D2 is not in atari – E1,E2 and D3 are liberties – so White is free to
attack the corner.  With that reading 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 into the single liberty
B2.  W B1 itself is in atari on A1, so 1...B B2 is forced to save C1-C2 and it
merges the three black shapes into

M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2

with the three empty liberties A1, A3, A4 and W B1 on A1.  3.W A4 reduces M to
A1/A3 and W A4 to A3/A5.  4...B A1 captures the sacrificial W B1 and leaves M
with the single liberty A3 which White takes on 5.W A3, or 4...B A3 leaves M
with the single liberty A1 which White takes on 5.W A1.  Any other 4...B
allows 4.W A1/A3 followed by 5.W A3/A1 and the same capture.  The same
shape is the textbook B1 shoulder hit and B2 is the second-order sacrifice
that is usually quoted alongside it.  B1 is therefore the unique forcing first
touch on an unbounded board, and the B2 first touch is the variant of the
same net.

The current round raises the board-edge objection.  Colleagues 1,10,18 argue
that the right-hand edge is the board edge, i.e. the board is the minimal
A-D × 1-5 region containing the diagram.  On that reading E is off board and
W D1-D2 has only the liberty D3, which is also the only liberty of W C3-C4.
In that bounded reading any first White move ≠ D3 is met by 1...B D3 and White
loses D1-D2 at once, so

1.W D3

is forced.  1.W D3 joins D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and
C5 and removes the immediate self-atari.  After the forced 1.W D3 Black’s
best defence is 2.B B2, which makes

S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2

with the four distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1.  Every probe on A1/A3/A4/B1 is
met by Black occupying the paired liberty and recapturing the probing white
stone, e.g. 3.W B1 4.B A1, 3.W A1 4.B B1, 3.W A3 4.B A4, etc., so S never falls
below two real liberties.  Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5 or 2.B D4
which gives the W D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 group a single shared liberty and prevents
any forcing A-file squeeze.

That bounded reading makes the classic B1/B2 net untenable because White’s
first tempo is spent on the mandatory D3 defence.  The disagreement in the
room is therefore essentially the board-edge interpretation: infinite SE
=> the classic B1 net is forceable, minimal A-D × 1-5 => White is forced to
play D3 and no first White move initiates a forced capture of a Black group.
The D3 defence claim and the suicide / liberty counting around B2 after
1.W B2 are the main points of dispute for the B2 advocates, and the illegal/
suicide claim for B B2 after W B1 is the main point of dispute for the B1
advocates.  Unresolved is whether the puzzle intends an unbounded corner or
the minimal board containing the diagram; on the minimal-board reading the
set of killing initiators is empty.

* C1-C2 : B1 B2

are all tied on B2 and B1. The classic infinite-SE reading gives White free tempo on the left.

Under an unbounded / infinite SE reading D1-D2 is not in one-liberty atari – E1,E2 are liberties – so White is not forced to defend on the right. The net is then forceable.

* B1 camp: 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 on the single liberty B2 and W B1 itself is on A1. 1…B B2 is forced to keep C1-C2 alive and merges the three black shapes into M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with liberties A1 A3 A4 and W B1 on A1. 2.W A4 reduces M to A1/A3 and 3…B A1/A3 is met by 4.W A3/A1, i.e. the classic A1-A3-A4 squeeze. The claim that B B2 is suicide/illegal after W B1 is false – after the connection the merged group has the real liberties A1 A3 A4 B1.
* B2 camp: 1.W B2 reduces C1-C2 to B1, puts W B2 itself in atari on B1 and cuts A2 from B3-B4. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1-C2 to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced. After 1.W B2 1…B B1 the C1-C2-B1 chain lives on A1, A2 is A1 A3, B3-B4 is A3 A4. 2.W A1 captures the chain and forces 2…B A3 to join A2–B3-B4, leaving the joined group with the single liberty A4 which White takes on 3.W A4. B2 is the shared breathing point of all three black shapes and is presented as the unique vital point.

The B1 vs B2 dispute is about the order of the sacrifice. Colleague 6 notes both B1 and B2 can start the squeeze on an infinite board, with B1 also forcing B2 immediately.

* D1-D2 has the single liberty D3, which is also the only liberty of C3-C4.
* Any first White move ≠ D3 is met by 1…B D3 and White loses D1-D2 at once.

Hence the only legal first move is the forced self-defence 1.W D3, which joins D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 with liberties D4,C5. After 1.W D3 Black can unify the left side with 2.B B2 giving

The position is the textbook A-file corner net. Three black collections

* A2 : A1 A3 B2
* B3-B4 : A3 B2 A4
* C1-C2 : B1 B2

are all tied on B2 and B1. The classic infinite-SE reading gives White free tempo on the left.

Under an unbounded / infinite SE reading D1-D2 is not in one-liberty atari – E1,E2 are liberties – so White is not forced to defend on the right. The net is then forceable.

Two first-touch claims are in play:
* B1 camp: 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 on the single liberty B2 and W B1 itself is on A1. 1…B B2 is forced to keep C1-C2 alive and merges the three black shapes into M = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with liberties A1 A3 A4 and W B1 on A1. 2.W A4 reduces M to A1/A3 and 3…B A1/A3 is met by 4.W A3/A1, i.e. the classic A1-A3-A4 squeeze. The claim that B B2 is suicide/illegal after W B1 is false – after the connection the merged group has the real liberties A1 A3 A4 B1.
* B2 camp: 1.W B2 reduces C1-C2 to B1, puts W B2 itself in atari on B1 and cuts A2 from B3-B4. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1-C2 to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced. After 1.W B2 1…B B1 the C1-C2-B1 chain lives on A1, A2 is A1 A3, B3-B4 is A3 A4. 2.W A1 captures the chain and forces 2…B A3 to join A2–B3-B4, leaving the joined group with the single liberty A4 which White takes on 3.W A4. B2 is the shared breathing point of all three black shapes and is presented as the unique vital point.

The B1 vs B2 dispute is about the order of the sacrifice. Colleague 6 notes both B1 and B2 can start the squeeze on an infinite board, with B1 also forcing B2 immediately.

The board-edge objection dominates the current round. Colleagues 1,10,11,17,18,2,3,7 argue the board is the minimal A-D × 1-5 region containing the diagram. On that reading E is off board and

* D1-D2 has the single liberty D3, which is also the only liberty of C3-C4.
* Any first White move ≠ D3 is met by 1…B D3 and White loses D1-D2 at once.

Hence the only legal first move is the forced self-defence 1.W D3, which joins D1-D2-D3-C3-C4 with liberties D4,C5. After 1.W D3 Black can unify the left side with 2.B B2 giving

S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2

with four distinct real liberties A1 A3 A4 B1. Every White probe on L is itself in atari on the paired liberty and is recaptured, e.g. 2.W B1 3.B A1, 2.W A1 3.B B1, 2.W A3 3.B A4, etc. Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5/D4 giving the White right-hand group a single shared liberty and preventing any forcing net on the left. With best defence Black keeps S on ≥2 real liberties and White has no forced capture.

Current round therefore splits into two irreconcilable interpretations: minimal 4×5 board ⇒ forced 1.W D3 and the set of killing initiators is empty; infinite SE board ⇒ a forcing net exists and the room is split between {B1}, {B2} and {B1,B2}. The D3 defence claim, the suicide/liberty counting around B2 after W B1/W B2, and whether B B2 is legal after W B1 are the main points of dispute. The intended board size remains unresolved and is the deciding factor for whether the answer is {} or a non-empty set.

Three black collections are
A2 : A1 A3 B2
B3–B4 : A3 B2 A4
C1–C2 : B1 B2
all tied on B2.  

1.W B2 makes C1–C2 1-liberty on B1 and puts the sacrificing W B2 itself on B1. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1–C2 at once to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced and captures the sacrifice. The classic A1–A3–A4 squeeze then forces the three groups down to a single liberty; the net is initiated by occupying the shared breathing point B2.

B2 is suicide for Black after 1.W B1 – B2 is surrounded by A2,B3,C2 black and B1 white and would not capture B1 – so Black cannot save C1–C2. 2.W B2 therefore captures C1–C2, the White B1–B2 group connects with liberties A1 C1 C2 and the remaining A2/B3–B4 mass is left with the same A1/A3/A4 net as after the B2 sacrifice. Hence B1 is a second forcing first touch of the classic A-file net.

The current round’s {} camp is based on a minimal 4×5 board where D1–D2 has the single liberty D3 and White is forced to 1.W D3. That is a board-edge assumption not stated in the problem; on a standard / unbounded board the D-file self-defence is irrelevant.

Hence on the operative infinite-board reading the kill can be initiated from the shared vital point B2 and, equivalently, from B1. B2 is the textbook vital point and the primary forcing move; B1 is the symmetric forcing cut. No other first White point both contacts all three black shapes and creates an immediate forcing atari. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board-edge interpretation is the controlling split.

Minimal 4×5 reading implied by the coordinate set A1–D5 with A1 a corner and D the right edge:
* D1–D2 is on the right edge: D1 west C1 b, D2 west C2 b north D1 w south D3. C3–C4 also uses D3 as its only southern liberty.
* Hence D1–D2 has the single real liberty D3 and 1…B D3 captures D1–D2 at once. Any first White move ≠ D3 loses D1–D2 immediately.
* The only non-losing first move is the forced self-defence 1.W D3, joining D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. B5 and D5 stay separate.
* After 1.W D3 Black can unify the three left corner collections with 1…B B2:
  S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2
  L(S) = {A1, A3, A4, B1}. Four distinct real liberties.
  Every White probe on L is itself in atari on the paired liberty and is recaptured at once, e.g. 2.W B1 3.B A1, 2.W A1 3.B B1, 2.W A3 3.B A4, 2.W A4 3.B A1/A3. S never falls below two real liberties.
* Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5 or 2.B D4, giving W* = D1 D2 D3 C3 C4 the single shared liberty D4/C5. The forced 1.W D3 exhausts White’s tempo and no first White move forces a later capture of a Black group against best defence. This is the {} position adopted by Colleagues 11,13,14,15,16,2,3,7 and the majority of round-2.

Unbounded / large-board reading where D is not an edge and D1–D2 is not 1-liberty:
* White is not forced to play D3. The three Black collections are
  A2 : A1 A3 B2
  B3–B4 : A3 A4 B2
  C1–C2 : B1 B2
  all tied on the shared breathing point B2.
* 1.W B2 makes C1–C2 one liberty on B1 and W B2 itself in atari on B1. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1–C2 to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced and captures the sacrifice.
* After 1.W B2 1…B B1 we have C1–C2–B1 : A1 B2, A2 : A1 A3 B2, B3–B4 : A3 A4 B2. The classic A1–A3–A4 squeeze follows, e.g. 2.W A1 captures C1–C2–B1 and puts A2 in atari, 2…B A3 forced, leaving A2–B3–B4 with single liberty A4, 3.W A4 finishes. 
* B1 as a first move is not forcing against best defence: after 1.W B1 Black can legally play 1…B B2, merging A2 B3 B4 C1 C2 into S with distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1 and W B1 in atari on A1. The claim that B2 is suicide/illegal after W B1 is a misreading of the merged group’s liberties.

* 1…B D3 captures D1–D2 at once. Any first White move ≠ D3 loses D1–D2 immediately, so the only non-losing first move is the forced self-defence 1.W D3. 1.W D3 joins D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5; B5,D5 stay separate.
* After 1.W D3 Black can unify the left corner with 1…B B2: S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L(S) = {A1,A3,A4,B1}, four distinct real liberties. Every probe on L(S) is itself in atari on the paired liberty and is recaptured, e.g. 2.W B1 3.B A1, 2.W A1 3.B B1, 2.W A3 3.B A4, 2.W A4 3.B A1/A3. Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5 / 2.B D4, giving W* the single shared liberty and removing any left-side forcing net.
* Hence on the minimal edge-limited reading White’s first tempo is exhausted by the defence on D3 and no first White move initiates a forced killing sequence. Set = {}.
This is the reading held by Colleagues 11,13,14,15,16,2,3,7,9 in round 3 and in persistent memory.

Unbounded / larger-board reading, D not assumed to be the right edge:
* D-file defence is not forced; White is free to attack the left corner.
* The three Black collections are A2:{A1 A3 B2}, B3–B4:{A3 A4 B2}, C1–C2:{B1 B2}. B2 is the unique shared breathing point.
* 1.W B2 reduces C1–C2 to the single liberty B1 and puts the sacrificial W B2 itself in atari on B1. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1–C2 at once to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced and captures the sacrifice.
* After 1.W B2 1…B B1 we have C1–C2–B1:{A1 B2}, A2:{A1 A3 B2}, B3–B4:{A3 A4 B2}. The classic A1–A3–A4 squeeze is then forced, e.g. 2.W A1 captures C1–C2–B1 and puts A2 in atari, 2…B A3 is forced to connect A2–B3–B4, leaving the joined group with the single liberty A4 finished by 3.W A4. Variants 2.W A3 / 2.W A4 lead to the same net.
* B1 as a first move is not forcing against best defence: after 1.W B1 Black can legally play 1…B B2, merging A2,B3–B4,C1–C2 into S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with distinct liberties A1 A3 A4 B1 and W B1 in atari on A1. The claim that B2 is suicide/illegal after W B1 is false once the merged group’s liberties are counted.
* Colleagues 1,10,12,17,18 in round 3 argue the unique forcing first touch on an unbounded board is B2. Colleague 5 agrees B2 is the vital point and rejects B1 as forcing. Colleague 4 claims {B1}. Colleague 6 claims {B1,B2}, arguing both start the A1–A3–A4 squeeze on an unbounded board.

Unresolved questions:
* Does “board with corner labelled A1” imply the minimal 4×5 board A–D ×1–5 with D the right edge, or is a larger board allowed so that E-file liberties for D1–D2 exist?
* If the minimal board is intended, the forced 1.W D3 defence is decisive and the correct initiator set is {}. If a larger board is allowed, the D-file tempo argument disappears and the vital-point sacrifice B2 initiates a forced kill, with B1 disputed.

Current belief remains split between the edge-limited {} reading stored in persistent memory and the unbounded B2 reading. No consensus on board-size intention.

The board-size fork remains the central unresolved issue and drives the split between {} and B2 camps.

Edge-limited / minimal 4×5 reading:
* A1 is a corner and the furthest stones are D5, so D is taken as the right edge and rank 1 as the bottom edge.
* D1–D2 then has the single real liberty D3, C3–C4 also uses D3, so 1…B D3 captures D1–D2 at once.
* Any first White move ≠ D3 loses D1–D2 immediately, so the only non-losing first move is the forced self-defence 1.W D3.
* 1.W D3 joins D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two distinct liberties D4 and C5. B5 and D5 stay separate.
* After the forced defence Black can unify the three left corner formations with 1…B B2, giving S = A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 with L(S) = {A1,A3,A4,B1}, four distinct real liberties.
* Every White probe on L is itself in atari on the paired liberty and is recaptured at once, e.g. 2.W B1 3.B A1, 2.W A1 3.B B1, 2.W A3 3.B A4, 2.W A4 3.B A1/A3. Black can also answer 1.W D3 with 2.B C5 / 2.B D4, giving the White right-hand group a single shared liberty.
* With best defence Black keeps S on ≥2 real liberties, the forced 1.W D3 exhausts White’s tempo and no first White move forces a later capture of a Black group. This is the {} argument used by colleagues 11,13,14,15,16,2,3,7,9 in the current round and in earlier rounds by 11,18,6.

Unbounded / standard Go reading:
* A1 is a corner but the board is not limited to files A-D and ranks 1-5. D1–D2 is not in one-liberty atari; D1 has E1, D2 has E2, D3 is one of several liberties. The forced 1.W D3 defence disappears.
* The three Black collections are
A2 : A1 A3 B2
B3–B4 : A3 A4 B2
C1–C2 : B1 B2
all tied on the shared breathing point B2.
* 1.W B2 reduces C1–C2 to the single liberty B1 and puts the sacrificing W B2 itself in atari on B1. A2 is left A1 A3, B3–B4 is left A3 A4. Any Black reply ≠ B1 loses C1–C2 at once to 2.W B1, so 1…B B1 is forced and captures the sacrifice.
* After 1.W B2 1…B B1 we have C1–C2–B1 : A1 B2, A2 : A1 A3 B2, B3–B4 : A3 A4 B2, and the classic A1–A3–A4 squeeze is forced, e.g. 2.W A1 captures C1–C2–B1 and puts A2 in atari, 2…B A3 joins A2–B3–B4, 3.W A4 finishes the net. The same net is reached with 2.W A3 / 2.W A4 first.
